claims.claim: Xenobot/anthrobot papers funded by Allen Frontiers Group/Allen Family Foundation and DARPA (plus NSF); anthrobots by Templeton and NIH.
claims.source_says: PNAS 2020: DARPA HR0011-18-2-0022, Paul G. Allen Family Foundation, NSF CBET-0939511. PNAS 2021: DARPA, Allen Frontiers Group 12171. Adv Sci 2023: John Templeton Foundation 62212, NIH S10 OD021624.
claims.note: All four Crossref records reproduce; DARPA award number is printed differently in 2021 and Sci Robot records, a minor variant.

claims.claim: Allen Discovery Center at Tufts was founded by the Paul G. Allen Frontiers Group; Tufts Now amount inconsistent ($10M vs up to $30M over eight years).
claims.source_says: Center page: "was generously founded by support from The Paul G. Allen Frontiers Group." Tufts Now: "$10 million grant"; "centers at Tufts and Stanford each will receive up to $30 million over the next eight years."
claims.note: Both pages say what is claimed, including the two differing figures.

claims.claim: No peer-reviewed demonstration of optogenetic control of ciliary beating in Xenopus found; multiciliated-cell optogenetics targets anchoring; ChR2 cilia claim only an unread patent snippet.
claims.source_says: Far-red light (740 nm) disrupted rootlet tilting, revealed by shortening of the apparent rootlet length.
claims.note: The cited paper does support the anchoring-not-beating part (and has no channelrhodopsin mention), but the negative literature claim and the patent snippet are not checkable from it.

overall: Funding and Allen Center claims reproduce from Crossref and Tufts pages. The optogenetics claim is only partly checkable: the paper supports the anchoring finding, while the absence claim is a search-limited negative.
